comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C47-C53, C93) on divergence time estimates. OpenEval finds the estimates SUPPORTED with convergent mitochondrial and nuclear data, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning molecular clock reliability and requesting fuller consideration of potential inaccuracies in genomic-based divergence estimates.

Perfect claim overlap (C71-C72, C74-C75, C77-C79) on morphometric analyses. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes quantified accuracy (98.2%) and appropriate acknowledgment of limitations, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall praise for thoroughness and convincing taxonomic revision.

Strong claim overlap (C37, C66, C109-C110) on new radiocarbon dates. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency and independent laboratory confirmation, while peer reviewers accept without specific critique.

Partial claim overlap (C33, C40, C68) on phylogenetic placement outside Equus. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging mitochondrial and nuclear evidence with systematic testing of alternatives, while peer reviewers praise thoroughness of phylogenomic analysis and accept the phylogenetic placement without challenge.

Partial claim overlap (C7, C35, C59) on taxonomic revision and genus designation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on phylogenetic, morphometric, and nomenclatural evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether phylogenetic placement alone justifies new genus designation and requesting comparative divergence data for other genus pairs.

Partial claim overlap (C5, C36, C76, C89) on single-species status and taxonomic revision. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites combined molecular and morphological evidence, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through praise for convincing taxonomic revision without challenging single-species conclusion.

Strong claim overlap (C94-C97, C107) on molecular-fossil dating discordance. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the model is speculative with untested predictions, while peer reviewers explicitly request fuller consideration of potential inaccuracies in genomic-based divergence estimates, indicating insufficient treatment.

Partial claim overlap (C80-C81) on single-species molecular evidence. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses lack of phylogeographic structure and holotype molecular data limitations, while peer reviewers accept single-species conclusion as part of overall convincing taxonomic revision.

Minimal claim overlap (C114) on extinction causation and synchronous timing. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN noting speculative inference about causal mechanisms, while peer reviewers find SUPPORTED, accepting the inference from radiocarbon dating and geographic distribution as reasonable interpretation.

Minimal claim overlap (C42) on critique of previous studies. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes systematic addressing of why previous studies differed strengthens results, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through acceptance of new phylogenetic placement.

Minimal claim overlap (C124-C125) on convergent evolution interpretation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval discusses methodological significance and broader implications, while peer reviewers accept as logical consequence of phylogenetic results without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates geographic and temporal distribution claims (C23, C28-C31, C63-C65, C67) as SUPPORTED, distinguishing confident palaeogenomic from tentative morphological identifications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates reproductive isolation inferences (C115-C120) as UNCERTAIN, noting extrapolations from extant species patterns without direct tests. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds molecular diagnostic characters for Haringtonhippus (C69-C70) SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caveats about limited sampling. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
